text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds rose to sharp gains in late trade following a sharp rise in U.S. Treasuries in the wake of tame consumer inflation data which dealers expect to set a positive tone for the market this week. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.81, up 0.90 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts shot higher on Tuesday, as did most major bond markets, closing nearly a point higher and itching to go further as long as Wednesday's raft of data do not prove disruptive. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-24/32, up 29/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures climbed on Tuesday as a smaller than expected rise in US inflation in March sparked a rally in major bond markets. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.02 up 0.76 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held to higher levels in late afternoon chased bunds and T-bonds higher after tame U.S. March CPI data pushed U.S. bonds up and underpinned an across the board bond market rise, dealers said. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.99 up 0.82 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were higher at midmorning after tame CPI data. Relief rally on tame CPI seen setting positive tone all week. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-21/32, up 31/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.08 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Tuesday's Tokyo session slightly higher after trading in a narrow range. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.63, up 0.17 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - Primary market activity was confined to just a few issues on Tuesday morning but each managed to differ in terms of the credit and/or structure from the next.
Russia announced plans for a second dollar Eurobond through the office of First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais.
A statement quoting Chubais said the issue would have a maturity of at least five years and be lead managed by J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg.
Russia's debut Eurobond, a $1.0 billion offering last November, was heavily oversubscribed.
